title: Die Lebenszeit
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 176. Text from Wikisource (twice proofread against the original). 1857 spelling preserved (daß, gieng, erwiederte, Creatur).
about: A brief fable in which God assigns each creature its years of life, and the donkey, dog, and monkey each beg to give up part of their share, which the ungrateful man claims for himself. The result is the tale’s real point: a wry accounting of a human life’s seventy years as thirty good years of one’s own, followed by the donkey’s, the dog’s, and the monkey’s borrowed years. Short and moralizing, it sits closer to a proverb than a story.

sentences.t: Als Gott die Welt geschaffen hatte und allen Creaturen ihre Lebenszeit bestimmen wollte, kam der Esel und fragte „Herr, wie lange soll ich leben?“
sentences.l: When God had created the world and wanted to appoint for all creatures their life-time, there came the donkey and asked “Lord, how long shall I live?”
sentences.i: When God had made the world and was about to fix the span of life for every creature, the donkey came and asked, “Lord, how long am I to live?”
sentences.n: Creaturen is the 1857 spelling of Kreaturen. Lebenszeit is literally “life-time”, the years allotted to a creature — the word the whole tale turns on. The tale begins at the creation, with no “Es war einmal”.

sentences.t: „Dreißig Jahre,“ antwortete Gott, „ist dir das recht?“
sentences.l: “Thirty years,” answered God, “is that right for you?”
sentences.i: “Thirty years,” God answered. “Does that suit you?”
sentences.n: ist dir das recht — literally “is that right to you”: the dative dir names the person the arrangement has to suit.

sentences.t: „Ach Herr,“ erwiederte der Esel, „das ist eine lange Zeit.
sentences.l: “Ah Lord,” replied the donkey, “that is a long time.
sentences.i: “Ah, Lord,” the donkey replied, “that is a long time.
sentences.n: erwiederte is the 1857 spelling of erwiderte, replied.

sentences.t: Bedenke mein mühseliges Dasein:
sentences.l: Consider my toilsome existence:
sentences.n: Bedenke is the imperative of bedenken, to think a thing over. Dasein (da + sein, “being there”) is one’s existence, the life one has to lead.

sentences.t: von Morgen bis in die Nacht schwere Lasten tragen, Kornsäcke in die Mühle schleppen, damit andere das Brot essen, mit nichts als mit Schlägen und Fußtritten ermuntert und aufgefrischt zu werden!
sentences.l: from morning till into the night to carry heavy loads, to drag grain-sacks into the mill, so that others eat the bread, with nothing but blows and kicks to be encouraged and freshened up!
sentences.i: carrying heavy loads from morning till far into the night, hauling sacks of grain to the mill so that others may eat the bread — and to be encouraged and refreshed with nothing but blows and kicks!
sentences.n: The complaint has no finite verb at all: it is a string of infinitives (tragen, schleppen, … zu werden) listing what his existence consists of. ermuntert und aufgefrischt, “encouraged and freshened up”, is bitter irony for a beating.

sentences.t: erlaß mir einen Theil der langen Zeit.“
sentences.l: remit me a part of the long time.”
sentences.i: let me off part of that long span.”
sentences.n: erlassen takes a dative of the person and an accusative of what is remitted: jemandem etwas erlassen, to let someone off something. Theil is the 1857 spelling of Teil.

sentences.t: Da erbarmte sich Gott und schenkte ihm achtzehn Jahre.
sentences.l: Then God took pity and made him a present of eighteen years.
sentences.i: Then God had pity on him and made him a gift of eighteen years.
sentences.n: schenken is to give as a gift — and what is given is release: the eighteen years are struck off the donkey’s span, not added to it.

sentences.t: Der Esel gieng getröstet weg und der Hund erschien.
sentences.l: The donkey went away comforted, and the dog appeared.
sentences.i: The donkey went off consoled, and the dog appeared.
sentences.n: gieng is the 1857 spelling of ging; weggehen is separable, and the particle stands at the end — gieng … weg.

sentences.t: „Wie lange willst du leben?“ sprach Gott zu ihm, „dem Esel sind dreißig Jahre zu viel, du aber wirst damit zufrieden sein.“
sentences.l: “How long do you want to live?” spoke God to him, “for the donkey thirty years are too many, but you will be content with them.”
sentences.i: “How long do you wish to live?” God said to him. “For the donkey thirty years are too many, but you will be satisfied with them.”
sentences.n: sprach (of sprechen) introduces speech all through the tale where English would simply say “said”. dem Esel is a dative of the person concerned: for the donkey, in the donkey’s case.

sentences.t: „Herr,“ antwortete der Hund, „ist das dein Wille?
sentences.l: “Lord,” answered the dog, “is that your will?
sentences.i: “Lord,” the dog answered, “is that your will?
sentences.n: Everyone in this tale addresses God with the familiar du — dein Wille, your will.

sentences.t: bedenke was ich laufen muß, das halten meine Füße so lange nicht aus;
sentences.l: consider what I must run — my feet do not hold that out so long;
sentences.i: think what running I have to do; my feet will not endure it that long;
sentences.n: aushalten is separable: halten … aus, to hold out, endure. Its object das stands first, and the verb second.

sentences.t: und habe ich erst die Stimme zum Bellen verloren und die Zähne zum Beißen, was bleibt mir übrig als aus einer Ecke in die andere zu laufen und zu knurren?“
sentences.l: and once I have lost the voice for barking and the teeth for biting, what remains left over to me but to run from one corner into the other and to growl?”
sentences.i: and once I have lost my voice for barking and my teeth for biting, what is left me but to trot from one corner to another and growl?”
sentences.n: habe ich erst … verloren is a conditional without wenn: the verb comes first and carries the sense “once I have …”. übrig bleiben — to be left over.

sentences.t: Gott sah daß er recht hatte und erließ ihm zwölf Jahre.
sentences.l: God saw that he was right and remitted him twelve years.
sentences.i: God saw that he was right and let him off twelve years.
sentences.n: recht haben — to be right, to be in the right; daß is the 1857 spelling of dass.

sentences.t: Darauf kam der Affe.
sentences.l: Thereupon came the ape.
sentences.i: Then the ape came.
sentences.n: der Affe covers ape and monkey alike; nothing in the tale decides between them.

sentences.t: „Du willst wohl gerne dreißig Jahre leben?“ sprach der Herr zu ihm, „du brauchst nicht zu arbeiten, wie der Esel und der Hund, und bist immer guter Dinge.“
sentences.l: “You surely want gladly to live thirty years?” spoke the Lord to him, “you do not need to work, like the donkey and the dog, and are always of good cheer.”
sentences.i: “You will be glad enough to live thirty years, I take it?” the Lord said to him. “You have no need to work, as the donkey and the dog do, and you are always in good spirits.”
sentences.n: wohl turns the question into an assumption — “I take it that …”. guter Dinge sein is a fixed phrase with the genitive: to be in good spirits.

sentences.t: „Ach Herr,“ antwortete er, „das sieht so aus, ist aber anders.
sentences.l: “Ah Lord,” answered he, “it looks so, but is otherwise.
sentences.i: “Ah, Lord,” he answered, “that is how it looks, but it is otherwise.
sentences.n: aussehen is separable — sieht … aus, looks; the subject das carries over silently into the second clause.

sentences.t: Wenns Hirsenbrei regnet, habe ich keinen Löffel.
sentences.l: When it rains millet-porridge, I have no spoon.
sentences.n: Wenns = wenn es. Hirsenbrei is millet porridge, a poor household’s dish; the line is proverbial — the good fortune falls, and the one it falls on has no means of catching it.

sentences.t: Ich soll immer lustige Streiche machen, Gesichter schneiden damit die Leute lachen, und wenn sie mir einen Apfel reichen und ich beiße hinein, so ist er sauer.
sentences.l: I am always to make merry pranks, cut faces so that people laugh, and when they hand me an apple and I bite into it, then it is sour.
sentences.i: I am always to be playing merry tricks and pulling faces to make people laugh, and when they hand me an apple and I bite into it, it is sour.
sentences.n: Gesichter schneiden — literally “to cut faces”, that is, to pull faces. hinein beißen is separable: beiße … hinein, bite into it.

sentences.t: Wie oft steckt die Traurigkeit hinter dem Spaß!
sentences.l: How often the sadness sticks behind the fun!
sentences.i: How often sorrow lies hidden behind the jest!
sentences.n: hinter etwas stecken — to lie behind something, to be what is really there; the shared entry for steckt gives only the plain sense “sticks, puts”.

sentences.t: Dreißig Jahre halte ich das nicht aus.“
sentences.l: Thirty years I do not hold that out.”
sentences.i: Thirty years of it I could not endure.”
sentences.n: aushalten again, split across the clause: halte … aus. The shared entry for halte was written for the imperative of plain halten and is not this word.

sentences.t: Gott war gnädig und schenkte ihm zehn Jahre.
sentences.l: God was gracious and made him a present of ten years.
sentences.i: God was merciful and made him a gift of ten years.
sentences.n: gnädig, gracious, comes from die Gnade, grace — the same root that gives the Gnade Eve appeals to in other tales of God walking the earth.

sentences.t: Endlich erschien der Mensch, war freudig, gesund und frisch und bat Gott ihm seine Zeit zu bestimmen.
sentences.l: At last appeared the man, was joyful, healthy and fresh, and asked God to appoint him his time.
sentences.i: At last man appeared, joyful, healthy and fresh, and asked God to fix his span for him.
sentences.n: der Mensch is the human being, man as a kind, not one particular man. Endlich stands first and pushes the verb into second place, so the subject follows it.

sentences.t: „Dreißig Jahre sollst du leben,“ sprach der Herr, „ist dir das genug?“
sentences.l: “Thirty years shall you live,” spoke the Lord, “is that enough for you?”
sentences.i: “Thirty years you shall live,” said the Lord. “Is that enough for you?”
sentences.n: sollst here announces an allotment rather than giving an order: you are to live so long.

sentences.t: „Welch eine kurze Zeit!“ rief der Mensch, „wenn ich mein Haus gebaut habe, und das Feuer auf meinem eigenen Herde brennt: wenn ich Bäume gepflanzt habe, die blühen und Früchte tragen, und ich meines Lebens froh zu werden gedenke, so soll ich sterben!
sentences.l: “What a short time!” cried the man, “when I have built my house, and the fire burns on my own hearth: when I have planted trees that blossom and bear fruit, and I think to grow glad of my life, then I am to die!
sentences.i: “What a short time!” cried the man. “When I have built my house and the fire burns on my own hearth; when I have planted trees that blossom and bear fruit, and I am looking to take joy in my life — then I am to die!
sentences.n: der Herd is the hearth, the fire-place of a house, and keeps its old dative -e (auf meinem eigenen Herde). meines Lebens froh werden takes the genitive: to grow glad of one’s life.

sentences.t: o Herr, verlängere meine Zeit.“
sentences.l: o Lord, lengthen my time.”
sentences.i: O Lord, lengthen my span.”
sentences.n: verlängere is the imperative of verlängern, to make longer (lang, long).

sentences.t: „Ich will dir die achtzehn Jahre des Esels zulegen“ sagte Gott.
sentences.l: “I will add on for you the eighteen years of the donkey,” said God.
sentences.i: “I will put the donkey’s eighteen years on top for you,” said God.
sentences.n: zulegen is separable, to add on, put on top. The 1857 text prints no comma before sagte — its punctuation of speech is lighter than modern German’s.

sentences.t: „Das ist nicht genug“ erwiederte der Mensch.
sentences.l: “That is not enough,” replied the man.
sentences.n: erwiederte again for “replied”; the 1857 spelling keeps the -ie-.

sentences.t: „Du sollst auch die zwölf Jahre des Hundes haben.“
sentences.l: “You shall have the twelve years of the dog as well.”
sentences.i: “You shall have the dog’s twelve years too.”
sentences.n: des Hundes is a genitive standing after its noun, where English puts the possessive in front: the dog’s years.

sentences.t: „Immer noch zu wenig.“
sentences.l: “Still always too little.”
sentences.i: “Still too little.”
sentences.n: immer noch — “still”, literally “always yet”. The line has no verb and no speech tag; the man is simply answering back.

sentences.t: „Wohlan,“ sagte Gott, „ich will dir noch die zehn Jahre des Affen geben, aber mehr erhältst du nicht.“
sentences.l: “Well then,” said God, “I will give you the ten years of the ape besides, but more you do not receive.”
sentences.i: “Very well,” said God, “I will give you the ape’s ten years into the bargain, but more you shall not have.”
sentences.n: Wohlan is an old and elevated “well then”. mehr erhältst du nicht puts the object first for weight, with the verb still standing second.

sentences.t: Der Mensch gieng fort, war aber nicht zufrieden gestellt.
sentences.l: The man went off, but was not satisfied.
sentences.i: The man went away, and yet was not contented.
sentences.n: zufrieden stellen, to satisfy, is still written as two words in 1857; the shared entry for gestellt covers only plain stellen, to place. The bargain ends with the man dissatisfied — which is the tale’s whole point.

sentences.t: Also lebt der Mensch siebenzig Jahr.
sentences.l: Thus man lives seventy years.
sentences.i: And so man lives seventy years.
sentences.n: Also is “thus, so”, never the English “also”. siebenzig is the older form of siebzig, and Jahr stands in the singular after a numeral, as German still does with measures.

sentences.t: Die ersten dreißig sind seine menschlichen Jahre, die gehen schnell dahin; da ist er gesund heiter, arbeitet mit Lust und freut sich seines Daseins.
sentences.l: The first thirty are his human years, they go quickly away; then he is healthy [and] cheerful, works with pleasure and rejoices in his existence.
sentences.i: The first thirty are his human years, and they pass quickly by; in them he is healthy and cheerful, works with a will, and takes joy in being alive.
sentences.n: The 1857 text prints gesund heiter with neither comma nor und between the two adjectives; the “[and]” in the literal line is supplied in square brackets and is not in the German. sich freuen takes the genitive: seines Daseins.

sentences.t: Hierauf folgen die achtzehn Jahre des Esels, da wird ihm eine Last nach der andern aufgelegt: er muß das Korn tragen, das andere nährt, und Schläge und Tritte sind der Lohn seiner treuen Dienste.
sentences.l: Hereupon follow the eighteen years of the donkey; then one load after another is laid upon him: he must carry the grain that nourishes others, and blows and kicks are the wages of his faithful services.
sentences.i: Then follow the donkey’s eighteen years, in which one burden after another is laid on him: he must carry the corn that feeds others, and blows and kicks are the wages of his faithful service.
sentences.n: auflegen is separable and here passive: wird … aufgelegt, is laid on; ihm is the dative of the person it falls on. The donkey’s own complaint is being paid back to man word for word.

sentences.t: Dann kommen die zwölf Jahre des Hundes, da liegt er in den Ecken, knurrt und hat keine Zähne mehr zum Beißen.
sentences.l: Then come the twelve years of the dog; then he lies in the corners, growls and has no teeth any more for biting.
sentences.i: Then come the dog’s twelve years: he lies about in the corners, growls, and has no teeth left for biting.
sentences.n: zum Beißen — “for biting”, an infinitive used as a noun with zu dem. It is exactly what the dog asked to be spared.

sentences.t: Und wenn diese Zeit vorüber ist, so machen die zehn Jahre des Affen den Beschluß.
sentences.l: And when this time is past, then the ten years of the ape make the conclusion.
sentences.i: And when that time is over, the ape’s ten years bring up the end.
sentences.n: den Beschluß machen — to form the conclusion, to close the series; Beschluß is the 1857 spelling of Beschluss.

sentences.t: Da ist der Mensch schwachköpfig und närrisch, treibt alberne Dinge und wird ein Spott der Kinder.
sentences.l: Then man is weak-headed and foolish, gets up to silly things and becomes a mockery of the children.
sentences.i: Then man is weak in the head and foolish, gets up to silly antics, and becomes a thing for children to mock.
sentences.n: schwachköpfig is literally “weak-headed”. ein Spott der Kinder werden — to become the children’s mockery, the object of their scorn. The tale closes flat, with no moral and no blessing.

glossary.gestellt: zufrieden stellen — satisfied (past part.; nicht zufrieden gestellt: not contented)
glossary.halte: aushalten — (I) hold out, endure (1st sg., separable: halte … aus; not the imperative of plain halten)
glossary.leben: leben — to live (infinitive; here the verb, not the noun das Leben, life)
glossary.steckt: stecken — lies, is hidden (3rd sg.; hinter etwas stecken: to lie behind something)
